column1: Table 13 Illustrative costs for a DDCC:VS Cost category Key cost drivers and considerations Ongoing/all phases → Coordination of personnel to develop and maintain relevant partnerships → Conducting an impact assessment and developing new policies, processes and standard Governance operating procedures for ongoing monitoring of use and impact → Independent oversight and monitoring → Personnel to oversee the overall programme until planned end (if there is one), including project management – and vendor management, if applicable → System set-up and end-user support Management and staffing → Monitoring feedback and taking corrective action → Handling complaints and exercising data subject rights, including legal redress Development and setup → Building completely new COVID-19 systems or leveraging existing software systems (e.g. adapting EIR systems) → Subscriptions, licensing fees and implementation costs associated with the software model Technology adaptation → Custom configurations or any enhancements, if needed, or any custom-developed software → Translations and localizations, if needed Deployment → Data storage (e.g. costs for storage in the cloud, or on local servers or individual devices) Equipment and hardware → Devices (e.g. printers and scanners) needed at the vaccination site or in the back office → Quality assurance, end-user testing and testing of conformity with standards and Testing interoperability with other systems (if part of the design); ensure costs are allocated for collecting end-user feedback and updating the digital system according to feedback received → Training vaccinators, health facility managers and data entry personnel, which may involve Training travel or other logistical costs → Training materials for verifiers of DDCC:VS → Transport of any necessary hardware, software or materials (including paper cards) to the Roll-out vaccination sites or certificate-issuance sites → Increased technical support required during the roll-out phase → Communications on when, where and how people can obtain a DDCC:VS → Communication of what DDCC:VS can and cannot be used for → Battling “infodemics” (too much information, misinformation and disinformation) associated Outreach and raising awareness with DDCC:VS → Meeting accessibility requirements of individuals and reaching groups with disadvantages, such as individuals with digital skill barriers or disability barriers Integration and interoperability → Adapting content, depending on acceptance agreements between Member States Establishing trust frameworks → Coordination for establishing agreements between Member States → Undertaking mapping exercises and adopting standards agreed upon through the Interoperability with other establishment of trust frameworks systems → Any licensing fees associated with use of standards (note that the standards proposed by WHO in this guidance document have no licensing fees) Scale → With the Paper First approach: printing, which will increase as more people are vaccinated Printing and, subsequently, more people receive a physical vaccination certificate
